newsitem.title: USA: M.L. Cass sees C$466 mln value with deal.
newsitem.headline: M.L. Cass sees C$466 mln value with deal.

text.p: M. L. Cass Petroleum Corp said Wednesday its risk-adjusted present value is expected to rise to over C$466 million as a result of an agreement with Nelson Bunker Hunt.

The company said it has tentatively agreed to acquire Hunt's rights to exploration concessions in Australia, Pakistan and Turkey. The nine concessions cover over 11.6 million gross acres, with the Hunt stakes resulting in a net lease holding of 11.3 million acres.
Cass said Martin Petroleum & Associates of Calgary evaluated the prospective reserves of four of the nine blocks.

The four cover over 7.2 million acres, including 1.5 million in the Sind Province of Pakistan, 4.2 million in the Eromanga Basin of South Australia and 1.5 million in the Galilee Basin of Queensland, Australia.

In a report dated June 11, the firm estimates the risk adjusted prospective reserves of these four blocks at about 6 million barrels of oil and 720 billion cubic feet of gas. Martin's estimate of the risked present value of future cash flows after exploratory and development costs is $233 million or $8 per share fully diluted.

Cass said it estimates the five remaining blocks will double the total prospective reserves and increase the company's risked adjusted present value to over C$466 million, or C$16.00 per share, discounted at 15 percent.
Calgary-based Cass Petroleum said it will maintain its Canadian operations and will continue to develop the Acadia Valley Oil Project on the Saskatchewan-Alberta border.
This month, the company noted, it sold its 50 percent interest in the Acadia Valley Gas Plant and associated shallow natural gas production for C$1.8 million.
It said the proceeds were used to retire all its natural gas prepayment obligations and to further reduce debt.
